You came into the Cinder Expanse with the *Kobayashi IV* and a trail to follow. The chronicle does not record how the trail began, only where it led first: Hollow Spire, a station gone quiet. The berth lights were dead, the decks carried dust, and a fresh notice about water rationing was posted where anyone could read it. No one in charge, no one to complain to. Even so, you docked.

The chronicle also mentions Bleakhold Station, which you reached ahead of schedule and where you were handed a berth without a single question. Nobody gives a stranger a berth that easily unless they want to know where the stranger goes next. A dockhand steered carefully around you, and boots approached across the deck. You were being watched, and nobody tried to hide it very well.

Your one relationship so far is with Vance Oduya, the dockmaster at Hollow Spire. He is a man who scrolls berth logs and keeps track of cancelled moorings, and the rank on him reads dangerous, which seems fair for someone who knows where every ship has been. The bond between you stands at nothing so far. He pulled the logs for you, but that is cooperation, not trust. The chronicle records no vows sworn, so there is nothing to mark as kept or broken.

The revelations are modest but they point somewhere. Vance's logs showed that the tug pilot Tamsin Reyes recorded the courier's departure by hand, and that she flagged a heading wrong for any lane. She can be reached within the hour. Then Vance told you that three cancelled moorings were paid for by the Ascendancy and never used, which contradicts their claim that they were buying berths. Someone paid for ships that never came, and someone else wrote down a ship going where no ship should go. Neither fact explains the other yet.

So you stand at the dock office at Hollow Spire, in good health and good spirits, with your supplies full and your ship undamaged. Vance is closing up for the night, finishing a late supper alone at the counter, and the question hanging over the room is what he will do with the ledger. Reyes docks soon, if the warning holds. You have a heading that makes no sense and a payment that makes less, and one man who knows more than he has said.
